name: Smileys & Emotion
description: Every smiley, heart and emotion emoji with its real meaning. Tap to copy, or open a face to see how people actually use it in texts.
intro: Faces and hearts do most of the emotional work in a text message, which is why this is the group people look up most. A smile is rarely just a smile: 🙂 can read as polite or icy, 😭 is more often laughter than grief, and the color of a heart changes what it says.

Below is every emoji in the group, in Unicode order, from the grinning faces through cat and monkey faces to hearts and comic-style emotion marks. The ones with an underline have a full meaning page with examples, look-alikes and when not to send them.

name: People & Body
description: Hand gestures, body parts, people, professions and families. Copy any emoji, pick a skin tone, and read what each gesture means.
intro: This is the largest emoji group because most of its characters come in five skin tones and several genders. It covers hand gestures (the part people search for most), body parts, individual people, roles and professions, fantasy figures, sports, and couples and families.

Gestures are where meanings travel worst between cultures: a thumbs up, an OK sign or a pair of folded hands can be warm in one place and rude in another. The gesture pages explain those differences. Tiles here show the default yellow version; skin-tone variants are on each emoji's own page.

name: Animals & Nature
description: Animal, bird, sea life, bug, flower and plant emojis. Copy them in one tap and learn the slang behind the goat, snake, butterfly and more.
intro: Mammals, birds, reptiles, sea creatures, insects, flowers and plants. Many of these are used literally, for pets, trips and gardens, but a surprising number carry slang: 🐐 is praise for the greatest of all time, 🐍 calls someone a traitor, and 🥀 has become shorthand for melodramatic sadness.
Flowers have their own quiet code as well, with roses for romance, tulips for spring and soft affection, and wilted ones for disappointment. Every emoji in the group is listed below in Unicode order.

name: Food & Drink
description: Fruit, vegetables, meals, sweets and drinks emojis. Copy and paste any of them and see which food emojis carry a second meaning.
intro: Fruit, vegetables, prepared meals, Asian dishes, sweets, drinks and tableware. Most food emojis mean exactly what they show, and they are among the most used in captions, invitations and restaurant talk.

A handful are famous for double meanings: the peach and the eggplant stand in for body parts, the cherry and the corn have their own slang, and ☕ and 🍵 are about gossip as often as caffeine. Those pages explain the literal and the suggestive readings so you can tell which one you were sent.

name: Travel & Places
description: Travel emojis for maps, buildings, vehicles, weather, sky and time. Copy them for trip posts and learn what the moon, fire and sparkles really mean.
intro: Globes and maps, landscapes, buildings, every kind of vehicle, clocks, and the sky and weather set. Unicode files the sun, moon phases, stars, fire and water here, which makes this group far more expressive than its name suggests.
🔥 is praise, ✨ adds emphasis or irony, 🌚 is a knowing side-eye and 💧 is rarely about rain. The pages for those emojis cover the slang; the rest of the group is listed below for quick copy and paste.

name: Activities
description: Activity emojis for sports, games, celebrations, arts and hobbies. Copy party, trophy and game emojis and see what each one means in a message.
intro: Events and celebrations, award medals, sports, games, and arts and crafts. This is the group for birthdays, holidays, match days and game nights: 🎉 for congratulations, 🏆 for wins, 🎃 and 🎄 for the seasons.

Some have picked up meanings beyond the literal. 🧿 is worn as protection against the evil eye, 🎭 hints at two-faced behavior, and 🃏 marks someone as a wildcard. Every activity emoji is listed below in Unicode order.

name: Objects
description: Phones, tools, money, clothing, music and office emojis. Copy any object emoji and find out what the moai, crown and money wings mean.
intro: Clothing, sound and music, phones and computers, books and stationery, money, mail, tools, science, medicine and household things. It is the catch-all group, so it holds both the plainly literal (a paperclip) and some of the most loaded emojis in slang.

🗿 is a deadpan stare, 👑 crowns someone as the best, 💸 means money leaving fast, and 🧲 says someone attracts attention. The underlined tiles lead to full explanations; everything else can be copied straight from this page.

name: Symbols
description: Check marks, arrows, warning signs, zodiac signs, shapes and other symbol emojis. Copy and paste them and learn when each one is used.
intro: Signs, arrows, religious symbols, the twelve zodiac signs, media controls, math and punctuation, keycaps, letters and geometric shapes. These are the workhorses of lists, bios and announcements: ✅ for done, ❌ for no, ⚠️ for a warning, colored circles as status lights.
Because symbols replace words, small differences matter, such as ✅ versus ✔️ or ⛔ versus 🚫. The pages for the most used symbols explain those distinctions and how each one renders across platforms.

name: Flags
description: Every country flag emoji plus the pride, pirate, white and checkered flags. Copy any flag, see its two-letter code, or test yourself in the quiz.
intro: There are 258 country and region flags, three subdivision flags (England, Scotland and Wales) and a small set of plain and special flags such as the rainbow, transgender, pirate and checkered flags. Country flags are not single characters: each is a pair of regional indicator letters spelling the place's ISO code, which is why Windows shows two letters instead of a flag.

Use the list below to copy any flag. The most searched ones have their own page covering what the design represents and which flags it gets confused with. To practice telling them apart, try the flag emoji quiz.
